To understand the device performance, the device statistic data based on the conventional method (Control) and the interface reconstruction method is shown in Figure 5.4. Based on Figure 5.4, we attribute the PCE improvement of our cells to the increase of FF and Voc. The increase in Voc indicates the low non-radiative recombination inside the device after the treatment, which is consistent with the longer carrier lifetime observed in TRPL. The increase in FF reflects the low series resistance inside the device, which can be ascribed to a better energy band alignment after the treatment. After the interface reconstruction, we can obtain the n=2 phase pure 2D perovskite, which is the type II energy band alignment between the 3D perovskite and the spiro layer. In contrast to wide-bandgap type I band alignment that will block the holes to transfer and increase the resistance, the type II band alignment is favorable for the holes to transfer through. Therefore, with the phase pure n=2 2D perovskite, the device after the treatment would have less series resistance inside the device and higher FF compared to the conventional method. Figure 5.5 shows the stability results of the devices under MPP tracking and continuous 1-sun illumination at ~40 ºC. The regular structure PSC based on the 2D reconstruction method retains 80% of the initial PCE after 1,270 hours, while the control maintains 80% of the initial PCE after 420 hrs. We attribute the stability enhancement of the PSCs after the 2D reconstruction method to two reasons. Firstly, after the 2D reconstruction treatment, the residual PbI , which is 2 detrimental to the device’s stability, can be effectively removed as illustrated by the GIWAXS graph (Figure 2d) and the SEM image (Figure 3a). Secondly, the favorable type II band alignment and better passivation of the 2D reconstruction treatment facilitate faster carrier transfer as shown in TRS (Figure 4b), which can prevent charge accumulation at the interface. Therefore, the 2D reconstruction method leads to better PSC stability compared to the conventional 2D treatment. Page 32 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology Figure 5.5. The device stability test under continuous 1-sun illumination and MPP tracking In conclusion, we successfully achieved a clean and phase-pure 2D/3D perovskite interface with the 2D reconstruction method, based on Le Chatelier’s principle and surface purification. The consequent n = 2, 2D perovskite layer, leads to a favorable type II band alignment between the perovskite and HTL layers, facilitating hole transfer from the 3D perovskite to the HTL. In addition, the formed 2D/3D junction displays enhanced interface passivation, with a 47% increase in carrier lifetime compared to the control.
